source.title: Depthwise Hyperparameter Transfer in Residual Networks: Dynamics and Scaling Limit
source.authors: Blake Bordelon; Lorenzo Noci; Mufan Bill Li; Boris Hanin; Cengiz Pehlevan

record.tranche_reason: The study compares depthwise training-loss behavior across residual parameterizations and finds that the proposed residual scaling improves transfer; it refines the depth-related claim but does not test training classification error directly.
record.gate_note: The paper reports training-loss results across depth and learning rates. These bear on V3's depth-related optimization outcome. It does not report training classification error, and its residual-branch scaling comparison does not directly test identity shortcuts.
record.test_reason: The study tests hyperparameter transfer across width and depth under different residual parameterizations. This does not measure any stated version: it does not compare plain and residual networks' training classification error, activation-matched initializations in plain networks, stability-threshold dynamics, or matched training with and without BatchNorm. Failure of learning-rate transfer alone does not establish depth degradation under V3.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors report consistent hyperparameter transfer across width and depth in tested residual architectures and support it with a proposed joint infinite-width-and-depth feature-learning limit. Their derivations use physics-level rigor, and most experiments last 10–20 epochs. This conclusion concerns transfer, rather than a direct test of V3.
record.recipe_differences: The study tests residual-branch scaling combined with µP and measures hyperparameter transfer through training-loss curves. It does not directly reproduce the claim's training-classification-error measurement.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported transfer behavior varies with residual scaling and normalization choice; standard µP transfers across width but not depth, while the proposed 1/√L scaling is reported to transfer across both.

fits_no_version.finding: Unscaled µP transfers learning rates across widths but fails across depths; scaled residual branches improve depthwise transfer, including in normalized residual architectures.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Residual-branch scaling combined with µP can make optimal hyperparameters more consistent across network widths and depths.

fits_no_version.finding: Appendix M reports approximate learning-rate transfer for both 1/L and 1/√L scaling with zero-initialized branch readouts, but increasing depth improves early training loss monotonically only with 1/L scaling.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Depthwise hyperparameter transfer does not guarantee that deeper residual networks achieve lower early training loss; this depends on branch scaling and initialization.

record.problems: Most experiments were limited to 10–20 epochs; the paper states that its theoretical results are at the rigor level of physics rather than formal proof. The relevant plotted values are figure-only in the supplied text.
record.rows_left_out: No other plotted training-loss results were extracted, including the ViT, ImageNet, momentum, feature-learning-rate, weight-decay, and depth-width trade-off experiments; they report hyperparameter transfer or loss rather than the specific depth-versus-shortcut behavior in V3.

untested.parts: Zero or near-zero training classification error in convolutional networks on CIFAR-10/100, including random labels and the stated recipe qualifications.
Spurious local minima and the benefit of extra student neurons in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems.

Training classification-error degradation in deeper plain batch-normalized CNNs, its persistence with longer training, its prevention by identity shortcuts, and the specified tanh and Fixup exceptions.
Activation-matched initialization and signal preservation improving learning speed or trainable depth in plain networks, including orthogonal-versus-Gaussian comparisons.
Loss recovery, curvature changes, edge-of-stability dynamics, and divergence relative to a measured stability threshold.
BatchNorm's effect on accuracy gain and learning-rate tolerance in matched networks, and Fixup's speed and stability relative to normalized residual networks.

record.verdict_notes: The supplied text contains the record's E2 supporting statements in Section 3 despite the automated excerpt-match failures. References to known normalization benefits are attributed to prior work and do not supply a matched BatchNorm-speed experiment here.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error, CIFAR-100, corrupted or random labels, model size, early stopping, and regularized recipes.
Teacher-student ReLU networks, spurious local minima, and student width relative to teacher width.

Classification error; direct plain-versus-identity-shortcut comparison; whether longer training leaves plain networks at higher error. The study compares training loss under residual scaling and normalization.
Comparisons of activation-matched, orthogonal, or Gaussian initializations and their effects on learning speed or trainable depth.
Learning rates above a stability limit, curvature or sharpness dynamics, and divergence relative to that limit.
Whether batch normalization speeds accuracy gains or increases learning-rate tolerance, and whether Fixup matches normalized training speed and stability.

rows.subject: ResNet + µP
rows.operation_detail: Sweep learning rate across depth and width with the standard residual parameterization.
rows.note: The figure compares depths and widths; the text states that µP transfers across widths but not depths. Missing datapoints indicate divergence.
rows.check: Figure 1(a) measures learning-rate transfer among residual networks, not V3's training-error comparison. Normalization is absent, as specified in Section 3. Figure B.2's caption explicitly states that all depth-30 runs under unscaled µP diverged.

rows.subject: 1/√L-ResNet + µP
rows.operation_detail: Sweep learning rate across depth and width with residual branches scaled by 1/√L.
rows.note: The text says the networks transfer over both width and depth; this is a learning-rate-transfer result, not a reported classification-error result.
rows.check: Figure 1(b) measures learning-rate transfer under the proposed parameterization, not V3. Normalization is absent. Successful transfer does not establish zero training error or the effect of adding identity shortcuts.

rows.subject: ResNet + µP, BatchNorm
rows.operation_detail: Sweep learning rate across depth with BatchNorm after the convolutional layer.
rows.note: The paper says normalization can slightly improve trainability across depths in standard ResNets; runs above target loss 0.5 were omitted from the plot.
rows.check: Figure 2(a) measures transfer among BatchNorm residual networks. Its depth color scale spans 18–318; the listed depths 18, 26, 34 and widths 512, 1024, 2048 belong to appendix plots and are not established for Figure 2. Losses above 0.5 are omitted, so displayed curves are selected.

rows.subject: 1/√L-ResNet + µP, BatchNorm
rows.operation_detail: Sweep learning rate across depth with residual branches scaled by 1/√L and BatchNorm after the convolutional layer.
rows.note: The paper says transfer is more reliable with 1/√L scaling; runs above target loss 0.5 were omitted from the plot.
rows.check: Figure 2(b) measures transfer, not V3. The caption specifies branch scaling of 3/√L, rather than exactly 1/√L. Its depth scale spans 18–318; the listed widths are not established for this figure. Losses above 0.5 are omitted.

rows.subject: ResNet + µP, LayerNorm
rows.operation_detail: Sweep learning rate across depth with LayerNorm.
rows.note: The paper says normalization can slightly improve consistency across depths in standard ResNets.
rows.check: Figure B.4(a) measures learning-rate transfer in LayerNorm residual networks. It provides neither a plain-network control nor training classification error, so 'partial' is not a state supported for V3.

rows.subject: 1/√L-ResNet + µP, LayerNorm
rows.operation_detail: Sweep learning rate across depth with residual branches scaled by 1/√L and LayerNorm.
rows.note: The paper says consistency is more reliable with 1/√L scaling.
rows.check: Figure B.4(b) measures learning-rate transfer under residual scaling with LayerNorm. More consistent transfer does not measure the depth-versus-shortcut effect named in V3.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
